pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 산 아래 마을에 삼형제가 살았어요. 첫째는 키가 껑충 크고, 둘째는 몸이 동글동글했지요. 그리고 막내는 몸이 반쪽이었어요. 팔도 하나, 다리도 하나. 그래서 이름도 반쪽이랍니다. 그리고 이 반쪽이는 마을에서 제일 날래고, 제일 힘이 셌답니다.
pages.t: Long, long ago, in a village at the foot of a mountain, there lived three brothers. The eldest was tall as a beanpole, and the second was round as a ball. And the youngest had half a body. One arm, one leg — and so his name was Banjjogi, the Half-Boy. And this Banjjogi was the quickest and the strongest boy in the whole village.

pages.ko: 반쪽이는 껑충 한 번에 담을 넘고, 껑충 두 번에 마당을 가로질렀어요. 어른도 겨우 드는 절굿공이를 한 손으로 번쩍 들어 올렸지요. "껑충! 껑충! 반쪽이가 간다!" 형들은 눈이 휘둥그레졌다가 괜히 툴툴거렸답니다. "얘, 좀 천천히 다녀!"
pages.t: One hop and Banjjogi was over the wall; two hops and he was clear across the yard. The heavy wooden pestle that grown-ups could barely lift, he swung up high with one hand. "Hop! Leap! Here comes Banjjogi!" His brothers' eyes went wide as saucers — and then they grumbled for no good reason at all. "Hey, slow down a bit, would you!"

pages.ko: 그러던 어느 날 아침, 마을이 발칵 뒤집혔어요. 밤새 누가 쌀뒤주를 열고 쌀을 몽땅 퍼 갔지 뭐예요. 지난밤에도, 그 지난밤에도요. 밤새 꽹과리를 꽹꽹 두드려 봐도 소용이 없었지요. "산에 사는 커다란 호랑이 짓이야!"
pages.t: Then one morning the whole village was in an uproar. In the night someone had opened the rice chest and scooped out every last grain. The night before too, and the night before that! They banged the little gong all night long — kwaeng, kwaeng — but it did no good at all. "It's that great big tiger who lives up the mountain!"

pages.ko: 첫째와 둘째가 팔을 걷어붙였어요. "우리가 가서 호랑이를 쫓아낼게요!" 반쪽이도 얼른 따라나섰지요. "나도 갈래!" 그러자 형들이 손사래를 쳤어요. "넌 어머니랑 집을 지켜. 산길이 얼마나 험한데." 반쪽이는 입을 삐죽 내밀었답니다.
pages.t: The eldest and the second rolled up their sleeves. "We'll go and drive the tiger away!" Banjjogi jumped up to go along too. "I want to come!" But his brothers waved him off. "You stay and look after Mother and the house. The mountain path is far too rough." Banjjogi stuck out his lip.

pages.ko: 하지만 반쪽이가 가만있을 리 없지요. 반쪽이는 마당에 앉아 볏짚을 비벼 새끼줄을 길게 길게 꼬았어요. 어머니는 반짇고리를 열어 터진 저고리를 꿰매 주었지요. "조심히 다녀오렴." "금방 다녀올게요!"
pages.t: But of course Banjjogi was not going to sit still. He sat down in the yard and twisted rice straw round and round into a long, long straw rope. Mother opened her sewing basket and stitched up his torn jacket. "Go carefully, now." "I'll be back in no time!"

pages.ko: 반쪽이는 새끼줄을 어깨에 둘러메고 산으로 뛰어올랐어요. 바위에서 바위로, 골짜기에서 골짜기로. "껑충! 껑충! 반쪽이가 간다!" 새벽에 떠난 형들을, 반쪽이가 어느새 바짝 따라잡았지요.
pages.t: Banjjogi slung the straw rope over his shoulder and went bounding up the mountain. From rock to rock, from valley to valley. "Hop! Leap! Here comes Banjjogi!" His brothers had set off at dawn — and before long Banjjogi had very nearly caught up with them.

pages.ko: 산 중턱에 이르자 나무 위에서 소리가 났어요. "사, 살려 줘!" 첫째와 둘째가 소나무 가지에 대롱대롱 매달려 있지 뭐예요. 나무 아래에는 집채만 한 호랑이가 어슬렁어슬렁 돌고 있었지요. "어흥, 언제까지 붙어 있나 보자!"
pages.t: Halfway up the mountain, a sound came from up in a tree. "H-help!" There were the eldest and the second, dangling from a pine branch! And down below the tree, a tiger as big as a house was pacing round and round. "Rrrrowr! Let's see how long you can hang on!"

pages.ko: 그때 반쪽이가 덤불에서 껑충 뛰어나와 호랑이 앞에 딱 섰어요. 호랑이가 코웃음을 쳤지요. "요만한 게 겁도 없구나!" "내기하자! 네가 나를 잡으면 쌀을 더 가져가고, 못 잡으면 다시는 마을에 내려오지 않기!" 호랑이는 수염을 씰룩였어요. "그쯤이야, 어흥!"
pages.t: Just then Banjjogi came leaping out of the bushes and planted himself right in front of the tiger. The tiger snorted. "A little scrap like you, and not one bit afraid!" "Let's make a bet! If you catch me, you may take more rice. If you can't catch me, you never come down to the village again!" The tiger twitched his whiskers. "Easy as anything. Rrrrowr!"

pages.ko: 반쪽이가 껑충 뛰자 호랑이가 우당탕 쫓아왔어요. 바위 뒤로 껑충, 나무 사이로 껑충, 덤불 밑으로 쏙! "껑충! 껑충! 반쪽이가 간다!" 호랑이는 헉헉, 혀를 빼물고 헐떡였답니다.
pages.t: Banjjogi went hopping away and the tiger came thundering after him. Hop, behind a rock! Hop, between the trees! And whoosh — under a bush! "Hop! Leap! Here comes Banjjogi!" The tiger huffed and puffed, with his tongue hanging right out.

pages.ko: 반쪽이는 미리 나무 사이에 새끼줄을 빙 둘러 두었어요. 쫓아오던 호랑이 뒷발이 줄에 턱! "형들, 지금이야! 당겨!" 나무 위에 있던 형들이 얼른 뛰어내려 줄을 잡아당겼지요. 영차! 영차! 호랑이는 소나무에 칭칭 감겨 옴짝달싹 못 하게 되었답니다.
pages.t: Banjjogi had already strung his straw rope round and round between the trees. The tiger came charging along behind — and his back paws caught in the rope! "Brothers, now! Pull!" The brothers up in the tree jumped straight down and hauled on the rope. Heave! Heave! The tiger was wound round and round the pine tree, and could not budge an inch.

pages.ko: "미안해… 산에 먹을 게 하나도 없어서 그랬어." 커다란 호랑이 눈에 눈물이 그렁그렁 맺혔어요. 반쪽이는 잠깐 생각하더니 매듭을 스르르 풀어 주었지요. "다시는 밤에 뒤주를 열지 마. 배고프면 낮에 와서 말해." 호랑이는 고개를 꾸벅하고, 도토리와 밤을 한 아름 굴려 놓고 산으로 돌아갔답니다.
pages.t: "I'm sorry… there was nothing left to eat up on the mountain." Great tears welled up in the big tiger's eyes. Banjjogi thought for a moment, then loosened the knots and let him go. "Don't open the rice chest at night any more. If you're hungry, come in the daytime and say so." The tiger bowed his head, rolled out a whole armful of acorns and chestnuts, and went back up the mountain.

pages.ko: 삼형제가 마을로 내려오자 사람들이 꽹과리를 치며 달려 나왔어요. 꽹꽹! 꽹꽹! 첫째가 반쪽이 어깨에 팔을 두르고 큰 소리로 외쳤지요. "우리 막내가 해냈어요!" 둘째도 신이 나서 함께 외쳤어요. "껑충! 껑충! 반쪽이가 간다!" 마을 아이들이 따라 외치며 깔깔 웃었답니다.
pages.t: When the three brothers came down to the village, the people came running out, banging the little gong. Kwaeng, kwaeng! Kwaeng, kwaeng! The eldest put his arm round Banjjogi's shoulders and shouted out loud, "Our little brother did it!" The second joined in, cheering away. "Hop! Leap! Here comes Banjjogi!" And all the village children shouted it after him, laughing and laughing.

pages.ko: 저녁이 되자 어머니가 반짇고리를 열고 삼형제의 옷을 나란히 놓고 꿰맸어요. "다음엔 같이 가자." 형들이 반쪽이 어깨를 툭 부딪쳤지요. "그럼! 형들이 줄을 당겨 줘야 하니까." 반쪽이가 씩 웃었어요. 반쪽이는 반쪽이 아니었어요. 처음부터 하나로 온전한, 우리 반쪽이였답니다.
pages.t: That evening Mother opened her sewing basket and laid all three brothers' clothes out side by side to mend. "Next time, let's go together." His brothers bumped their shoulders gently against Banjjogi's. "Of course we will! Somebody has to pull the rope for me." Banjjogi grinned. Banjjogi was not half of anything. He had been whole, all of one piece, from the very beginning — our own Banjjogi.
